brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Not built on purpose: it would hold a hot iron, and these parts are 3D-printed plastic. The configurator can't check heat resistance.

requirements.requirement: Sits on the bench as one unit
requirements.evidence: The two bases are joined by jointBolt:0#0,0#0. check_build passed with no rule errors and the meshes clear.

finish.summary: I built the two bins but left out the iron holder. A holder for a switched-on soldering iron would hold something hot, and these parts are 3D-printed plastic. The configurator only checks fit and knows nothing about heat resistance, so I won't design that part. The build is two full bases bolted together. One has a full-depth bin for solder and the other a 3-compartment bin for spare tips. The check passed with no rule errors and the meshes clear. For the iron, use the metal stand that came with it or a commercial heat-rated one, set apart from this organiser.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
